conviction_note: Arithmetic on management's own Q2-call guide (NIM +7-9bp off 3.58% adjusted, ~$50M expense run rate, tax under 20%) lands at about $0.83, which is where consensus sits, so the quarter itself carries no edge. The small positive lean comes from a bar cut 2.6% in 30 days, a stock down 8.9% since the last print while SPY rose 3.4%, a first-ever buyback approved after the quarter closed, and short interest that has risen for three straight settlements. Against that, Nashville peer FBK and Independent Bank both reported deposit costs up 6bp and Regions reported deposits down 1.2%. p_up 55 on abs 4.0 gives +0.4. impact_sum +0.8 is larger only because the small positives were sized one by one; the two numbers agree in sign.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS $0.83 (post 2-for-1 split), revenue about $173M (Zacks via search summary; AAII, 3 analysts, $0.83, https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/516802-what-you-need-to-know-about-servisfirst-bancshares-incs-q3-earnings). Earnings Whispers has $0.82 EPS and $175.6M revenue (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/SFBS). Consensus was revised 2.62% lower over the last 30 days. Two sources agree within $0.01, so the bar counts as sourced. Comparison: Q2 2026 EPS was $1.57 before the split, $0.785 after it (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001430723/000117184326004772/exh_991.htm). The company gives no numerical guidance; the margin guide comes from the Q2 call.
positioning_check: Short interest was 6,161,384 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 5.6% of 109.35M shares outstanding (float is smaller because insiders hold a lot). That is up from 5.66M on 09-15 and is the third straight rise. Days to cover 7.49, against a 12-month range of 5.86-15.04 (https://equibles.com/stocks/sfbs/shortinterest). Elevated for a bank but not the 18-23%-of-float squeeze territory. No usable option chain (baseline options.status empty_chain), so there is no skew. Tape: run_up_20d -6.88%, 5d +0.79%, 14.7% below the 52-week high; AAII has the stock -8.9% since 2026-07-20 against SPY +3.4%.

findings.finding: Management's own Q2-call guide implies a Q3 at about consensus. The CFO guided NIM expansion of 7-9bp next quarter off a 3.58% adjusted Q2 NIM, slowing to 4-6bp after that, with $2.2B of fixed-rate cash flows over 12 months repricing from 5.22% toward a 6.32% new-loan rate. He called the ~$50M expense run rate stable and targeted a tax rate under 20% with tax credits in H2. Period-end Q2 loans were $533M above the Q2 average, which lifts the Q3 average balance. My arithmetic (NII about $161-163M, fees about $12M, expense $50.5M, provision about $11M, tax 19%, about 109.4M diluted shares) gives about $0.83, the consensus number, so this lands inside guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NIM and EPS beats have been paid: 2026-01-20 +14.58% on a beat with margin expansion. 2025-10-20 -6.8% on an EPS and revenue miss plus credit. In-line prints moved +1.2% to +2.6% (2026-04-20, 2026-07-20).
findings.why_not_priced: It probably is priced. Consensus at $0.83 is what the guide produces. The only unpriced piece would be the size of the H2 tax-credit benefit: a tax rate 2-3 points lower adds about $0.02-0.03, which would show up as a consensus above $0.85 if analysts had fully modelled it.
findings.independence: Repricing and floor data come from the August 2026 investor presentation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001430723/000117184326005365/exh_991.htm), a separate company document that points the same way.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after SFBS last spoke show deposit competition building in the Southeast. FB Financial (Nashville, a market SFBS also serves) reported 2026-10-13: NIM down 12bp to 3.83%, total deposit cost up 6bp to 2.32%, loan yields flat. Independent Bank reported deposit costs up 6bp. Regions (Birmingham, SFBS's home market) reported 2026-10-16 with average deposits down 1.2% QoQ as large commercial clients moved balances off balance sheet. SFBS grew loans 15% annualized in Q2 on deposits up only 0.4% QoQ, and its guide assumes H2 seasonal deposit inflows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-10-20 print (-6.8%) included weak loan growth and a credit issue. No past SFBS print is documented as turning on deposit costs alone.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer proxy, and Regions' NIM rose 2bp, so the sector read is mixed. If this were priced into SFBS, consensus would sit below the guide-implied $0.83 rather than on it. The 2.6% estimate cut is consistent with a partial pricing.
findings.independence: Regions 3Q26 release (https://finviz.com/news/403470/regions-reports-earnings-of-611-million-and-eps-of-071-in-3q-2026): deposits down 1.2% but NIM up 2bp, so it is partly the same direction and partly opposed. This is a proxy, not an SFBS number.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, after SFBS management said on the July call that they expected no rate moves this year. The August presentation calls the balance sheet slightly liability-sensitive, and management quoted about -$240K of first-year NII per +25bp. That is trivial for Q3 EPS, but it may temper the margin narrative on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No past print is documented as turning on rate sensitivity.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike is public, and the sensitivity in the company's own disclosure is tiny, so this is mostly priced. The only unpriced part is how management frames Q4 NIM on the call.
findings.independence: Sensitivity figure from the Q2 call transcript (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2935469), a different document.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-14 the board approved the company's first-ever buyback, up to 2,000,000 shares (about 1.8% of the 109.35M shares) through 2027-12-31. That was 5 days before the print and after Q3 had closed, so the board knew the quarter. The release says the program reflects 'confidence in ServisFirst's financial strength, capital position and long-term growth prospects'. CET1 is 11.83%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior buyback. The stock moved only +0.79% over the 5 days that include the announcement.
findings.why_not_priced: The announcement is public and drew little reaction (5-day run-up +0.79%). What is not priced is what the timing implies: a first-ever authorisation from a board that already knew Q3 is weak evidence against a credit surprise. If the market read it that way, the stock would have re-rated toward its pre-July levels rather than sitting 14.7% below its high.
findings.independence: None. The CEO's July remark that buybacks were not 'off the table' (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2935469) is context, not corroboration.

findings.finding: The large real-estate-secured nonaccrual relationship (an analyst cited about $100M; NPAs were 0.96% of assets and nonaccrual loans $169.7M at Q2) is in disposal: on the Q2 call the CEO said the properties 'are being listed' and that all nonaccrual loans are 'properly reserved'. A Q3 sale near the reserved value would cut NPAs sharply; a sale below it would mean a charge-off. Q2 net charge-offs were 0.11%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This relationship (a multifamily credit) surfaced at the 2025-10-20 print, which fell 6.8% on a miss plus the NPA rise. Credit is a line this name moves on.
findings.why_not_priced: Neither the timing nor the recovery is public. A resolution already priced would have shown up as the stock regaining its post-January levels; instead it sits 14.7% below its 52-week high with negative estimate revisions. The outcome is genuinely two-sided, so it is sized near zero with a wide band.
findings.independence: Q2 release NPA figures and management's attribution of NPAs to one large relationship (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001430723/000117184326004772/exh_991.htm). That is the same company and a different document.

findings.finding: The bar has been lowered into the print. Zacks shows Q3 consensus EPS revised 2.62% lower in the last 30 days. AAII's revisions grade is 35 (Negative), with 1 downgrade and 1 upgrade last month. The consensus fair value tracked by Simply Wall St was cut 5.4% on 2026-10-06 on a 'slower loan growth outlook'. The stock is -8.9% since the July print against SPY +3.4%, yet the company's own guide still produces about $0.83.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-01-20 print came after a weak tape and rose +14.58% on a beat. The 2025-10-20 print fell on a miss in a regional-bank credit scare.
findings.why_not_priced: The underperformance is visible. What may not be priced is that the guide-implied number did not fall with the estimates: a print at or slightly above $0.83 now clears a bar that was cut. If the market expected a miss priced to that bar, the 20-day run-up would not be the only sign; it would also show up as a consensus below the guide.
findings.independence: Simply Wall St narrative update of 2026-10-06 (https://www.simplywall.st/narratives/r0eqylqj-sfbs-net-interest-margin-rebound-will-drive-future-upside-despite-recent-headwinds), a different aggregator.

findings.finding: Short interest has risen for three straight settlements to 6.16M shares (5.6% of shares outstanding) at 2026-09-30, with 7.49 days to cover. Shorts are building into a print that the company guide puts at consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest at prior prints is not known.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is not a fact the market misprices so much as fuel. At 5.6% it gives a modest asymmetric response to an in-line or better print, not a squeeze.
findings.independence: The same direction of sentiment shows in the estimate revisions (AAII), which is a different source but the same theme.

findings.finding: Industry loan growth stayed healthy through Q3: the Fed H.8 release of 2026-10-09 shows loans and leases growing about 9.0% annualized in August and 6.8% in September. That supports SFBS's 'record pipeline' and its loan-growth-driven NII.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loan growth surprises have mattered: the 2025-10-20 drop cited weak loan growth.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro proxy that has been public for 10 days and is broadly priced. It is filed small.
findings.independence: Regions 3Q26 shows business loans up 0.8% QoQ, so it is weaker but positive (https://finviz.com/news/403470/regions-reports-earnings-of-611-million-and-eps-of-071-in-3q-2026).

outside_window.finding: FINRA short interest for the 2026-10-15 settlement will not be published until 2026-10-26, after the window.

baseline_tension: The small positive lean cuts against the -6.88% 20-day run-up and the negative estimate revisions. There is no skew to oppose, and the rising short interest is moderate, so the lean is held at p_up 55.
lessons_applied: Rule 6, inside the guide: the guide-arithmetic finding lands inside what management guided, so it was cut from +0.4 to +0.2.
Rule 5, proxies: the peer deposit-cost finding was cut from -0.5 to -0.4 and the H.8 loan finding from +0.2 to +0.1, as proxies not confirmed by SFBS.
Rule 7, positioning: the bar-lowered finding was cut from +0.4 to +0.3 and the short-interest finding from +0.3 to +0.2, because 5.6% of shares out is not a crowded short.
Rule 1, verified fact versus reaction: the buyback is already on the wire and drew only a +0.79% 5-day reaction, so it was cut from +0.4 to +0.3.
abs_move_pct 4.0 and p_up 55 are unchanged, so expected_move_pct stays +0.4.
